content.text:
I submitted composition 221 (Cu 0.65, Fe 0.14, V 0.21), which had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 2.5×10⁻⁷ A.

| Index | Cu | Fe | V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 234 | 0.28 | 0.12 | 0.60 | 5.0×10⁻⁸ |
| 74 | 0.53 | 0.12 | 0.35 | 1.1×10⁻⁷ |
| 221 | 0.65 | 0.14 | 0.21 | 2.5×10⁻⁷ |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose with copper content. That matches what I expected: the light is 2.06 eV, and copper-rich vanadates have smaller band gaps, so they absorb more of it.
- **Library coverage:** 221 is at the copper-rich edge of the library, so there are no more copper-rich compositions to try.
- **Untested region:** I never measured the iron-rich part of the library (iron above 40%). The only merit budget was 3 measurements, and I spent them following the copper trend. So whether 221 is the best in the whole library is still unconfirmed.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. They report crystal structure, not photocurrent, so they couldn't add a measured candidate.
